He said: "I'm not one for sort of self-praise and stuff, but the thing I'm absolutely proudest of is the conversations that I’ve had with my boys and how they’ve dealt with it.

"For me, there's nothing more important than family, and you never know how you'll deal with something like this, right? To see how my family, my boys, and Annie have coped with this is definitely the thing that I'm proudest of without a shadow of a doubt. They approach it with the same energy and positivity as me, if not more."

Around 50 per cent of sufferers die within two to three years of diagnosis but Moody remains determined to live life to the full and raise more awareness and money to fund research in the quest for effective treatments and, eventually, a cure.

He added: "Progression [of his condition] remains slow for me. What I've seen over the last year and a bit is how different it is for everyone.

"Everyone's journey is slightly different. The harsh stats are that 50 per cent are gone within two to three years. But that means that 50 per cent aren't. I remain positive with that, as do my family. It's not that it's not difficult or sad, but no, I'm in a good spot at the minute."

Moody, who is yet to decide which route he will walk, intends to call on many of his rugby pals again. He said: "I absolutely loved the bike ride. Just the opportunity to be with mates again, doing something together that is challenging, all for a good cause, there's nothing better for me. I'll be trying to roll out as many of my old colleagues as possible.

"We just want as many people as possible. But it's not just about the walk. Not everyone will be able to give up the day on June 12. People will be able to get involved in this campaign in whatever way suits them."

Front Up: Walk the Coast's entry cost is £30 per person, with participants encouraged to aim to raise around £300 each. The campaign officially launches at England's Nations Championship match against New Zealand at Twickenham on Saturday. To sign up, visit frontup.org.uk.

title: Springboks rock World Rugby as Erasmus goes public with match-fixing question
article_text:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has sparked an extraordinary rugby row after raising the possibility of match-fixing and manipulation of results during an explosive assessment of World Rugby officiating in the international game.

The outspoken Springboks boss questioned whether World Rugby match officials who witness foul play but fail to intervene could be influencing the outcome of matches, following his side's defeat to France on Friday night.

Erasmus claimed there were as many as 17 knee-drop tackles committed against his players during the contest in Paris, none of which resulted in a sanction, and also questioned the handling of an incident involving Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast against Fiji.

His comments came ahead of South Africa's clash with Ireland this weekend, with Erasmus predicting that Prendergast would escape suspension despite describing his challenge as a "terrible" hip-drop tackle.

But it was his remarkable suggestion that officials could be manipulating results by failing to punish dangerous play that threatened to overshadow everything else.

Speaking to reporters in Dublin on Monday, Erasmus said: "I'm not saying he's wrong, I'm saying if he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing? Is that not interfering with the outcome of a game if you see this injury that happened there, a knee-drop tackle happened there, and it's been decided that knee drop tackles are out?"

He continued: "Now, I'm saying to you, my feeling is knee drop tackles is out. They happened 17 in our games. Not one was penalised even.

"And if the TMO didn't see it, maybe then technology must be better. If he saw it and he ignored it, what does that boil down to?

"Manipulation of the game or the result or injured players getting injured. So all I'm asking, don't take TMOs out and discourage them to get involved. Then the wrong team will win and players will get injured. That's all I'm saying."

When it was put to Erasmus that he was making a serious insinuation, the South African immediately insisted he was not accusing anyone of wrongdoing.

"It's not an accusation, it's not an accusation," he replied.

Nevertheless, his comments represent a remarkable intervention from one of rugby's most prominent coaches, particularly given the serious implications of questioning whether officiating decisions could amount to match-fixing.

Erasmus argued that the sport's emphasis on player welfare was being undermined by dangerous tackles going unpunished, while also expressing frustration at calls for television match officials to become less involved in games.

He claimed his analysis of the France defeat had identified 17 knee-drop tackles, of which he believed 11 warranted at least a penalty and three deserved yellow cards.

"Let's say 11 of those were, I thought, at least a penalty and three I thought were at least yellow card," he said. "And not one was sanctioned. And not one was showed out or cited."

Erasmus also claimed France scrum-half Maxime Lucu had spent only seven minutes in the sin bin rather than the required 10, adding to his frustration over the officiating.

He suggested that if officials had simply missed the incidents, those were mistakes. However, he repeatedly questioned what it would mean if they had seen dangerous play and consciously decided not to act.

The Springboks boss insisted his argument was about protecting players and ensuring the correct team won, rather than suggesting South Africa were being deliberately targeted.

title: 2026 Nitto ATP Finals Draw, Schedule & More
article_text:
The ATP Finals are underway at the Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy, with two Americans Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe, qualifying for the 2026 tournament.

title: Anna Kalinskaya is Engaged!

Anna Kalinskaya is leaving the singles field.

The 27-year-old Kalinskaya announced her engagement to businessman Tomas Ferrari in a joint Instagram post the couple made.

“Can’t wait for our next chapter,” the couple posted along with an engagement rink and red heart emoji.

Former world No. 11 Kalinskaya previously dated Jannik Sinner and was in the Italian’s box when he defeated Taylor Fritz to capture the 2024 US Open championship. Sinner climbed in the box and shared a celebratory kiss with Kalinskaya after his Flushing Majors triumph.

Previously, Kalinskaya was romantically linked to Nick Kyrgios. The owner of one of the game’s best two-handed backhands, Kalinskaya made Tennis Now’s Future Top 10 picks list back in 2024.

title: Alex Eala Marks Season End With Career Achievement
article_text:
Alex Eala put together a special, breakthrough year on the tennis court.

Her season is over as she rests and recovers while spending time with family, but amid the campaign’s conclusion, Eala also learned some special career news.

The Filipina tennis star, who won’t turn 22 until May, ends the year with her highest-ever world ranking.

The recent release of the Women’s Tennis Association rankings feature Eala as the No. 15 player in the world in WTA singles play.

She is the sixth-best under-23 player on the list.

Her 2026 season concluded with 2,392 rankings points, good for that 15th spot.

Eala used the words, “A fairytale ending to a fairytale season,” on her Instagram late in the year.

While some tennis diehards, as well as those from back home, knew Eala — this season was a historic rise.

She won her first WTA singles title at the D.C. Open in Washington.

Eala also won a WTA 125 title in Birmingham.

The talented lefty capped her season at the Hong Kon Open, where she finished as the runner-up to Claire Liu.

For the 2026 season as a whole, Eala went 47-26. She earned $2,087,795.

The one bummer to end the year for Eala was that an injury hampered her in the Hong Kong Open final.

She didn’t have any easy path to the final. She won in the first round 6-4, 6-3. In the next round, it was a 6-4, 7-6 (7) victory for Eala.

Eala needed another tiebreak in the quarterfinal in a 7-6 (7), 7-5 victory.

The semifinal went three sets for Eala, who eventually triumphed 7-5, 3-6, 6-4.

The final against Liu wasn’t Eala’s best, though, and she finished at less than 100% in a 3-6, 0-6 loss.

One loss to end a successful season won’t stop Eala’s drive, though, and she won’t enter next season as an unheralded sensation. She’ll have a target on her back.

Eala has already gained one of the largest followings in tennis. Everyone she plays will want to be the player that beats her.

title: Looking at Rory McIlroy's two-act career and PGA Tour cards being handed out and taken away
article_text:
Rory McIlroy's career has been analyzed, picked apart, applauded and criticized, yet even as he traverses into his late 30s, he continues to draw the attention of golf fans. This past weekend, McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai crown (fifth in a row), pulling him alongside Colin Montgomerie for the most all-time on the European circuit.

There is little doubt what McIlroy can do on the golf course, especially considering how long he has been doing it. After all, he has been ranked inside the top 20 of the Official World Golf Rankings since October 2009.

Let's restate that for dramatic purposes: McIlroy has been ranked inside the top 20 of the OWGR since October 2009. The top three players in the world at the time? Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson and Steve Stricker.

There is a common misconception in golf circles that longevity is not often appreciated or celebrated. The pendulum has largely swung too far in one direction on that ill-conceived talking point.

McIlroy has been the man for nearly two decades. Adam Scott, Justin Rose and many others have enjoyed long, successful careers and continue to put their best foot forward even into their 40s. This is the way the game is trending. Competitive players will emerge from their 20s, 30s, and yes, even their 40s. Heck, last week there was one still in his teens.

What is so compelling about McIlroy's arc, though, is not the consistency he has been able to blanket across his career. Rather, it is the windows in which he has summited the proverbial mountaintop and the number of times he has done so.

Let's have his Race to Dubai titles do the hard work for us to identify those periods.

From 2012-16, McIlroy claimed 17 worldwide victories consisting of three major championships, two World Golf Championships, two DP World Tour Championships, the Tour Championship, the BMW PGA Championship and the Irish Open. In that span, he claimed a FedEx Cup and three Race to Dubai crowns.

A decade later, he has accomplished something similar. From 2022-26, he had 15 worldwide wins, including two Masters, The Players Championship, the DP World Tour Championship, the Tour Championship, the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am and the Irish Open. In that span, he claimed a FedEx Cup and five Race to Dubai crowns.

Careers are made in pockets of greatness stretching anywhere from two to five years. It happens all the time in golf. What doesn't, though, is a second act like that being enjoyed by McIlroy, one equal in accomplishments but greater in grit.

It's just rare. For as much as experience can lift players past newcomers, there comes a time when it starts to weigh them down just as equally.

The decade-long major drought, the agonizing close calls and noise that followed him outside the ropes. It's buried stars before him and will bury those after him. But McIlroy managed, and he used it as fuel for a second act that rivals his first, proving that his real superpower isn't just how high his floor is, but how many times he's been able to reach his ceiling.

Ladies and gentlemen, welcome your class of 2026 DP World Tour graduates! These 10 men have all found new jobs on the PGA Tour for next year, except for ... wait a minute ... that guy looks familiar! Didn't he ... already?! Oh well, these players will all come stateside in 2027, including America's own Patrick Reed.

Reed's name may lead the way, but in terms of points, that honor goes to Eugenio Chacarra, who nearly won the Race to Dubai. Chacarra will be a fun one to watch next season and beyond as the 26-year-old Spaniard has an old-school energy and look to his game.

Reed and Chacarra have enough game to contend, compete and keep up with the players on the PGA Tour, but that has not always been the case since the DP World Tour started sending over its top 10 finishers, who were not otherwise exempt, from the Race to Dubai.

This current season has been the best effort since its inception with Kristoffer Reitan, Alex Noren and Jordan Smith all keeping their cards as John Parry and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen have a chance to as well in the last week of the PGA Tour season.

The 2026 PGA Tour season comes to an end this week at the RSM Classic once they finish the Austin Championship, which continues to be a complete nightmare for the Tour. The Tour chose to cancel play on Sunday due to rain and will wrap up the tournament on Monday before heading to Sea Island, Georgia, which is one of my favorite places on Earth.

I've always found it to be such a funny juxtaposition -- Sea Island and the stakes at hand. An easygoing, laid-back community welcomes the Tour into town for a week, during which some jobs will be secured, and others will be lost.

It will also be a clash of eras, as the young guns are the main attraction for those on-site looking to watch golf. Michael Brennan, Jackson Koivun, Blades Brown and Ben James headline the field with Billy Horschel, Chandler Phillips, Chris Kirk and Lee Hodges flirting with the top-100 cutoff.
